## Dispatch order — R35

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6391-last-merge-driver-row`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, verbatim across its two comments)

> Charter on unlock, exactly as the body frames it — **falsification attempt first**: sweep the whole `changeset-release.yml` for the merge family with a control term on every zero-hit; read `changesets/action@v1` itself for whether the version-branch update ever performs a local three-way merge or only force-pushes (the load-bearing question); confirm `git checkout -- .` is not a merge. Falsified ⇒ keep the row and record the firing path in the file. Confirmed ⇒ ship the whole unit together (last row + table + guide section + the `.gitattributes` `merge=pnpm-merge` line), which the bidirectional pins force anyway; #6358/PR #6367 and #6369/PR #6389 are the worked examples. This is dead-mechanism removal with the doc pinned both ways — **not a gate weakening**.

> Unlock: PR #6389 **merged at 19:48Z**, so the "zero live rows pending measurement" premise now exists on `main` — the table is down to the one `changeset-release.yml` row.

⛔ **The fold with #6392 is declined by this seat** — one card per agent. #6392 landed its own PR (#6423); ⛔ do not touch `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`.

### ⭐ Step 1 can end the task, and the load-bearing question is a marketplace action

Sweep the **whole** `changeset-release.yml` for the merge family (`merge`, `rebase`, `pull`, `cherry-pick`, `am`, `apply`, `revert`), ⚠️ **with a control term on every zero-hit** — a zero-hit with no control is not a reading, and this lane has been defeated by that three times in the last twelve hours.

Then the part that actually decides it: ⭐ **read `changesets/action@v1` itself.** Does its version-branch update ever perform a **local three-way merge**, or does it only **force-push**? A force-push resolves no merge, so a driver has no occasion to fire. That question is not answerable from the workflow file — you have to read the action.

⚠️ Also confirm, do not assume: `git checkout -- .` at ~`:1018` **discards working-tree changes; it is not a merge.** And `git config` at ~`:525–526` is the driver configuration itself, not an invocation.

- **Falsified** (any local merge on a path including `pnpm-lock.yaml`) → ⛔ **keep the row**, and **record the firing path in the file** so nobody re-derives this a fourth time. That is a successful run, not a failed one.
- **Confirmed** → ship the whole unit together.

### If confirmed, the unit is four things and the pins force it

1. the driver configuration in `changeset-release.yml`;
2. the last row of the **"Lockfile Merge Driver"** table;
3. the surrounding guide section, which describes a mechanism that would then have **zero** live rows;
4. ⭐ the `.gitattributes` line `pnpm-lock.yaml merge=pnpm-merge` — the last piece of a mechanism nothing exercises.

⛔ These cannot be split: `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` pins the doc against the workflows **in both directions**, and one of its assertions is explicitly *"keeps the `.gitattributes` half of the mechanism true"*. PR #6367 and PR #6389 are the worked examples — read both diffs before writing yours.

⚠️ **Framing that matters for review**: this is **dead-mechanism removal with the doc pinned both ways — not a gate weakening.** Say so in the PR body, and say what the table is down to.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6391 -b claude/issue-6391-last-merge-driver-row main && cd ../objectui-6391 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` was contended **five times** on the 25th and cost two rework rounds. No open PR holds it right now, but **fetch `main` and confirm that before your first edit to it**, and merge (⛔ never rebase, never force-push) if it moved.
- ⚠️ Run the **whole** `scripts/__tests__` tree. That page carries at least three separate pins and a subset chosen from your own subject matter misses the ones that fire on the page as a whole — that cost PR #6402 a round.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report. **Lead with the falsification attempt** — the sweep, the control terms, and specifically **what you found reading `changesets/action@v1`** — because everything else is conditional on it. Then the four halves and the `ci-cd-pipeline-doc` run.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6434), escalated as ruled. ⭐ The falsification attempt worked, in the direction that matters.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R35. Report returned `status: needs_decision`, `premise_still_valid: false`.

### This is the outcome the charter said was a success, and it was reached honestly

Triage's charter: *"Falsified ⇒ keep the row and record the firing path in the file."* ⭐ **Half the premise was confirmed and half falsified**, so nothing was deleted and the measurement was recorded. ⛔ The tempting version of this run — confirm the CI half, call the unit dead, ship all four deletions — would have broken a live contributor path, and every gate in the repo would have gone green while it did.

### The confirmed half, with the control terms I asked for

Every zero-hit paired with a control that **hit the same file**: `rebase` 0 vs `base` 2 · `cherry-pick` 0 vs `pick` 4 · `apply` 0 vs `app` 8 · `revert` 0 vs `rev` 5 · `git am` 0 vs `git ` 10. ⭐ And the 28 `merge` hits were **read, not counted** — 26 lines of prose about the version-PR merge plus the 2 config lines.

⭐ **The load-bearing reading is the one the workflow file could not answer, and it was actually taken**: `changesets/action@v1` cloned **at the tag** (v1.9.0 = `a45c4d594aa4e2c509dc14a9f2b3b67ba3780d0d`), with `src/git.ts` **and the executed `dist/` bundle agreeing line for line** — because the bundle is what runs, and a source-only reading would have proven nothing about the artifact. `prepareBranch` is checkout → `reset --hard` → commit → **force-push**. ⭐ And the decisive negative: the bundle **reads no `.gitattributes` and implements no merge driver at all** — isomorphic-git's `mergeTree`/`diff3` are not even bundled, only its error classes.

### ⛔ The falsified half — and the measurement design is what makes it trustworthy

`.gitattributes` has a **live consumer**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells contributors to configure this driver and then run `git merge upstream/main`. Proven in a scratch repo with **one variable changed** — attribute present → driver fires, lockfile regenerated; attribute absent, nothing else altered → `CONFLICT (content)` with markers in `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

⭐ Two design choices make that a measurement rather than a demonstration: the driver was a **marker script rather than `pnpm install`**, so firing is *observed* rather than inferred from a side effect; and it ran in **throwaway repos in the scratchpad, never in a worktree**, so there is no mutate/restore leg to get wrong.

### ⭐ It found the unit is six things, not the four the card scoped

Removing `.gitattributes` also falsifies the pin test's own *"keeps the `.gitattributes` half of the mechanism true"* assertion — so that describe block joins any removal — and `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s section becomes instructions for a driver no attribute can select. ⛔ A card that under-scopes its own removal unit by two files is exactly the thing to catch **before** the deletion, not after.

### Escalated rather than guessed — correctly

> That is a decision about a repo-wide contract, not a cleanup.

⭐ And the reason it must be a human's: option B relaxes an **anti-vacuity guard** that exists because a zero-match grep once made both directions vacuously green. ⛔ That is a gate-strength change, which this seat never self-adjudicates. Decision filed as **#6436** with four-axis analysis and a recommendation of **B**, including that cost stated as the reason it is not mine to take.

The deeper defect the dev named — ⭐ *"that model, not the row, is what blocks the removal, and it will block the next attempt the same way"* — is filed as **#6437** so it outlives whichever option wins.

### What the PR actually ships

The firing path recorded in the file, plus a correction: the row's stated reason (*"version bumps rewrite the lockfile on the release branch"*) is **measured false**, because a rewrite is not a merge. ⛔ Nothing deleted; `.gitattributes`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the pin test and `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` untouched. The pin test stays green **precisely because nothing was removed** — 34/34, both directions plus the `.gitattributes` assertion.

⭐ One gate check worth naming: `check:pre-install-import-graph` **derives its population from `changeset-release.yml`**, so the added comment block was directly implicated — and its verdict confirms the install boundary did not move. That is checking the gate your diff actually perturbs, not just the ones the card named.

### The second hand-back, filed

`check-pre-install-import-graph.mjs:273-278` and its test cite this workflow's driver line as **the** worked example of a quoted argument that must not be read as an install — an example PR #6389 already had to re-point **once**. ⚠️ Under option A or B it must be re-pointed again, and there would be **no real in-repo example left**; the test's fixture is inline, so it stays green either way — ⛔ **which is exactly why the stale comment would go unnoticed.** Recorded on #6436 as a connected cost of both live options rather than as its own card, since it has no independent resolution.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming PR #6434 on **every** check green — it deletes nothing and is correct under all three options. ⛔ The removal itself waits on #6436.
